newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Saturn plans Wellington phone network.
newsitem.headline: Saturn plans Wellington phone network.

text.p: Wellington-based cable tv company Saturn said on Thursday a $30 million injection from a new shareholder would enable it to launch an alternative phone network in Wellington within two years.
Saturn announced that Canadian telecommunications company SaskTel had agreed to invest NZ$30 million in the company in return for a 35 percent stake in the business.

"SaskTel brings valuable telephony expertise to Saturn as we migrate our business in New Zealand from a pure video operation to an integrated cable-telephony service," existing shareholder United International said in a statement.
Saturn already provides multi-channel television in the Hutt Valley and will launch a pay-per-view video service in the next few weeks.
Chief executive Jack Matthews said Sasktel would be an ideal investor and partner in developing the company's telephony operations.
"Saturn will complete the construction of an alternative telephone system to Telecom in Wellington within the next two years," he said in a statement.
